Serres Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Serres, Greece

Demolished. Jews have lived in Serres since at least the 12th century, though the Ottomans transferred most to Istanbul in 1453; the remaining Romaniot community dwindled as Sephardi immigrants predominated from the early 16th century onward, eventually replaced by a tight-knit Sephardi congregation that built a synagogue seating 2,000. The community peaked at 2,000 people in 1904, but the Balkan Wars, WWI-era emigration, and finally the arrest of 471 Jews in 1943 brought it to near-extinction — only a single Jew remained in Serres by 1983.
